isolation.command: docker compose --project-directory {{repoRoot}} exec -T postgres createdb -U bookshop -T bookshop {{isolationName}}
isolation.teardownCommand: docker compose --project-directory {{repoRoot}} exec -T postgres dropdb -U bookshop --if-exists {{isolationName}}

notes: createdb runs inside the running container, so no psql has to exist on the host.
Templating from the base database requires no active connections to it; when that fails the verdict falls back to REFUSE rather than writing to the shared database.

Deliberately mechanism none. SELECT isolates the keyspace but NOT pub/sub: a message published on database 10 reaches a subscriber on database 1, so channel names collide across every logical database.
Channel prefixing would be an application change, not an overlay knob. Any service that publishes here is refused unless the risk is accepted explicitly.

stateReview.notes: Applies pending migrations on startup, so every launch writes schema to whichever database it points at.

notes: This overlay runs in a container, so localhost would resolve to the container itself. The worktree compose file declares the base stack's network external, which keeps the base DNS names working unchanged. See references/discovery.md section 4.
verifyRequest targets localhost because curl runs on the host, where the overlay publishes its port.

stateReview.notes: Reads only, but subscribes to the shared channel, so an overlay would take deliveries away from the base indexer.

notes: The theft case in one entry: nothing is written, yet reusing the base subscription still breaks the base stack.

stateReview.notes: Browser client only: it reaches services over HTTP and holds no store credentials, so both lists are checked-empty rather than unknown.

notes: Not dockerized. Service URLs fall back to http://localhost:PORT in code, so it reaches the base stack with no config.
cp -Rc is an APFS clone: near-instant, near-zero disk, and each server keeps its own pre-bundle cache.

constraints.where: CORS_ORIGINS, set on every service in compose.yaml
constraints.effect: An overlay storefront on a port outside the allowlist gets 400 with no CORS header, while a health route still answers 200 — the browser only shows 'Failed to fetch'.
constraints.remedy: Add the port to the gitignored root .env before launching; verify by reading the response headers of a real cross-origin request.

catalog-api::events.reason: Stock-change events are published on a shared channel that cannot be isolated. Base-stack subscribers will see this overlay's events; accepted because the base stack is idle during this test.
